key_insight: Coupling teacher calibration with student learning can remove teacher bias in LLM distillation and drive the student toward the oracle student even without target-domain reward feedback.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical distillation strategy for domain-shifted deployment settings where labeled rewards are available only on source data but the student must generalize to target questions.
method: Calibrate the teacher using source-domain reward feedback at each iteration.
Train the student on target questions with token-level branching from the calibrated teacher.
Feed the updated student back into the next calibration step to progressively reduce bias.
evidence_signal: The paper provides a polynomial-rate convergence proof showing the student’s expected average KL divergence to the oracle student goes to zero, and also shows direct matching can remain bounded away from the oracle.
watch_item: The method depends on reliable source-domain reward feedback and iterative calibration, so performance may degrade if source rewards are noisy or the source-target shift is severe.
paper_title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
